beliefs.practice: When creating the Mongo client in Python, configure connection pooling and timeouts explicitly (e.g., pymongo.MongoClient(DOCUMENTDB_URI, maxPoolSize=100, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000, connectTimeoutMS=10000, socketTimeoutMS=20000, tls=True)).

Keep the cluster connection string and any keys out of source control and environment files by storing them in environment variables or a secrets store (e.g., AZURE_KEYVAULT or OS env var DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never write them to logs or files.

Use short-lived API keys or a managed identity where supported instead of long-lived primary keys; if Azure AD authentication is not available for Mongo API, rotate keys regularly and store rotation configuration in a secure store.
Handle 429 (ProvisionedThroughputExceeded) and other transient errors by implementing retries with exponential backoff and jitter; honor Retry-After headers returned by the server.

Provision throughput appropriately for vector/ANN workloads: use autoscale RU/s or increase dedicated RU/s for collections used for embeddings and nearest-neighbor queries to avoid frequent RU throttling.
Keep embeddings consistent: store an explicit embedding_dim field in each document, verify all vectors match the same dimension, and reject or normalize mismatched-dimension inserts at ingest time.
Create separate collections (or databases) for regulatory documents and internal policies, each with its own vector index and metadata fields, to simplify RBAC, quota, and index tuning.

Define explicit metadata fields (source, doc_id, section_id, jurisdiction, effective_date, embedding_version) on each document and index those fields used for filtering so semantic retrieval can be constrained efficiently.

When creating vector indexes, configure HNSW parameters (M, efConstruction) and search-time ef appropriately for your recall/latency tradeoff (e.g., M=16-64, efConstruction=200-400, efSearch tuned per workload) and test on representative data.

Also create supporting indexes for the common retrieval filters and sort patterns (e.g., compound index on {jurisdiction:1, effective_date:-1, score: -1} or partial indexes for frequently queried subsets) to avoid collection scans.

Store original text and small chunks in the same document as their embedding and an excerpt_id so you can return provenance without additional lookups; keep chunk size consistent and record chunk boundaries in metadata.

For seeding and tests, include a mode that loads documents without computing embeddings (seed_noembed) and creates empty vector fields and indexes, so developers can inspect collections without requiring API keys.

Use server-side projections to limit returned fields (exclude large embeddings where not needed) during query and retrieval to reduce network transfer and RU consumption (e.g., projection to {text:1, metadata:1}).

Measure RU consumption for representative RAG flows (embedding writes, ANN searches, and final context assembly) and optimize by batching writes, reducing returned fields, and tuning index/search parameters to control costs.
Enable logging and metrics collection (request charge, latency, 429 counts) and hook them into alerts so provisioning or query changes are driven by observed RU pressure and error patterns.

Protect PII and sensitive policy text by applying field-level encryption or encrypting text before storing it if regulatory/PII rules require it, and enforce least-privilege access to collections used for sensitive documents.

When using LlamaIndex or other RAG frameworks, cache embeddings and retrieval results where possible, and expire caches when underlying document collections or embedding models change, to avoid repeated embedding/API calls and RU charges.
Run explain plans (e.g., db.collection.find(query).explain('executionStats')) for your typical retrieval queries to ensure they use indexes and to validate expected RU usage before shipping.
Use idempotent upsert patterns or versioned documents (incrementing version or etag-like field) during re-ingest so re-running seed or sync jobs does not create duplicates and makes reindexing safe.
Limit the size of individual documents (keep chunks under recommended document size limits, e.g., well under 2MB) to avoid storage inefficiencies and high RU reads for single-document fetches.

When performing nearest-neighbor search, combine vector similarity with metadata filters server-side (post-filter or index-accelerated filter) to reduce false positives and RU cost of examining many candidates.

For CI and unit tests, use a small dedicated test database/collections with teardown (drop collections after tests) and avoid running tests against production sample_fintech_08 database; allow a seed_noembed fixture for test runs without API keys.

Design the RAG prompt composition to include provenance (source doc id, clause text, jurisdiction, effective_date) and include a link or retrieval id so generated compliance gap reports cite exact clause origins.

Avoid using admin/root keys in application code; create least-privilege Mongo users for the app with specific collection-level permissions where supported by the server and rotate credentials periodically.
Back up collections with point-in-time or scheduled backups for regulatory data and test restoration regularly; do not rely solely on retention in the cluster without export/backup copies.
